summary: Initial migration discovery with PulseAI: they currently use OpenAI hosted endpoints for most traffic, evaluating Dedicated Redwood for predictable throughput, lower per-token cost, and VPC/private deployment eventually. Main concerns: eval parity vs OpenAI, compatibility with vLLM/TGI stack, KV cache and prompt engineering differences, SOC2/KMS compliance and data residency. Agreed next steps: share pricing + security pack and run a technical benchmark with their prompt set.
topics: Model compatibility and eval parity (OpenAI -> Redwood dedicated)
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-11-24 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Alicia (CTO), Mark (Lead ML Eng), Priya (Infra), Devon (Product)
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, mic check?
[00:05] Alicia: yep, hi all, Alicia here from PulseAI, excited to talk through migration options

[00:10] Jordan: great. quick agenda: understand current stack, goals for migration, constraints (security/latency/cost), and then technical compatibility questions. Samira will jump into the deep bits
[00:20] Samira: hi team, quick intro: i'm Samira, solutions engineer at Redwood. i focus on perf, batching, and dedicated deployments
[00:28] Mark: hey, Mark. our immediate problem: costs and stability. OpenAI's hosted has been fine for prototyping but costs spike, and we need more predictable latency for 99th percentile requests
[00:35] Priya: also our security team wants more control of keys and network egress: so VPC or private deployment is on the table
[00:42] Jordan: totally. curious, what's your current throughput and model mix?
[00:47] Mark: mostly gpt-4 style prompts via OpenAI, about 200 reqs/s steady with spiky peaks to 700 reqs/s during batch tasks. embeddings are separate and heavy during nightly jobs
[00:58] Devon: product wants sub-300ms median latency for short chat turns, and < 800ms p95 ideally. we can tolerate higher for long-form generation

[01:10] Samira: ok that gives us a target. with Dedicated we usually size GPU pools to hit those p95 numbers: our autoscale and burst handles peaks. question: are you running any local vLLM or TGI for internal dev?

[01:20] Mark: we run vLLM in some infra experiments for cost optimization, but not in prod. main model calls go to OpenAI. we are evaluating if we can keep the same prompt engineering and eval metrics when moving to a dedicated runtime
[01:30] Jordan: makes sense. two key concerns we hear: eval parity (do the answers match) and integration friction (APIs, tokenization differences). we can run parity tests with your prompt set
[01:40] Alicia: exactly: we did some toy tests against open models and saw differences, particularly for domain-specific QAs. how do you approach model parity?

[01:48] Samira: short answer: we map model families and versions, run your eval set end-to-end, and tune model variants and temperature. also check tokenization differences and provide a report. often parity is achievable but requires iteration; we'll pin model versions for the pilot
[02:00] Mark: and what about my vLLM/TGI experiments? could we bring model artifacts from those systems to Redwood Dedicated?

[02:08] Samira: yes, you can. Redwood supports standard model artifact formats: we have guidance for converting TGI exports or vLLM checkpoints. caveat: kernel selection and quantization paths differ, so perf characteristics will change. we do test runs and recommend specific quantization profiles
[02:22] Priya: on the infra side, we need to know about network flows. will calls originate from our VPC? how does private deployment look from a KMS and audit perspective?

[02:30] Jordan: for Private we offer a customer-managed control plane or VPC peering options. keys can be managed via your KMS/HSM, and we can stream audit logs to your SIEM. samira, do you want to expand?

[02:40] Samira: sure: so private deployments can be configured with customer KMS for model and request encryption. we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and per-token auditing. logs can be routed to your log destinations. depending on the topology (VPC peering vs private agent), egress constraints differ
[02:55] Alicia: our compliance team will want SOC2 type 2 docs and network diagrams. can you provide those?
[03:00] Jordan: yes, we'll share the security pack: SOC2, ISO artifacts, threat model and network diagrams. i'll include them in the follow-up
[03:08] Mark: how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching? our chat agents rely heavily on cached prefixes to reduce latency and cost

[03:15] Samira: Redwood runtime manages KV caches per session. for Dedicated, we expose configs for cache TTL, sharding behavior, and memory allocation. also automatic prefix caching is configurable to balance cost vs latency. there can be small behavioural diffs vs openai: we'll document these
[03:30] Devon: for embeddings: are there any differences if we move from OpenAI embeddings to a hosted Redwood embedding model? similarity scores we rely on are quite sensitive

[03:38] Samira: embeddings vector spaces differ by model. we recommend running an embedding parity eval: take a sample corpus, compute similarity with current OpenAI embeddings, and compare downstream recall. often we can find a model/encoder combination that matches well
[03:52] Jordan: also worth noting we offer caching for embeddings and dedupe to reduce nightly job costs: can save significant $
[04:00] Mark: pricing: open question: how do costs compare? especially if we keep some calls to OpenAI while moving other to dedicated

[04:08] Jordan: we have hybrid routing options. you can route by policy: latency-sensitive to Dedicated, exploratory to hosted. pricing will depend on reserved capacity and burst settings. i'll include a few commitment tiers in the deck
[04:20] Priya: what about model rollouts and canarying? we need safe deploy paths for models with rollback

[04:26] Samira: Redwood supports canary deploys, A/B routing, and automated fallback to a compatible hosted model if dedicated encounters capacity issues. rollouts can be per-route and we track regressions via eval sets
[04:38] Mark: one technical worry: we use prompt templates with a lot of pre and post processing. do you support function/tool calling or structured outputs like we do with OpenAI?
[04:46] Samira: yes, we support streaming, function calling, and structured response enforcement. small syntax differences might exist but we provide SDKs to ease migration
[04:55] Alicia: curious about latency: how do 95th percentiles look on Dedicated? you mentioned autoscale but we need concrete numbers for a given GPU config

[05:03] Samira: for a 8xA100-ish pool tuned for chat-turns we typically see median ~120-250ms and p95 around 400-700ms depending on model and sequence length. we'll run a benchmark with your typical prompt lengths to give exact numbers

[05:20] Jordan: i'll propose a benchmark plan: we run an initial parity test (sanity checks) then a performance run that mirrors your traffic for 24-48h. Samira will run a small pilot and we'll compare cost and quality
[05:30] Mark: OK. what about model versioning: if we want to pin to a specific revision, is that supported?
[05:36] Samira: yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollback. plus model variants (quantized vs fp16) can be surfaced as compatible fallbacks
[05:45] Devon: integrations: does Redwood provide an SDK we can drop into our service to switch endpoints?
[05:50] Jordan: yes, SDKs and stable REST APIs: most customers swap endpoints and use Redwood routing policies for canarying. we also have terraform modules for infra automation
[06:00] Priya: regarding data residency: we need EU region for EU customers, do you have region controls?
[06:06] Samira: yes, we can pin deployments to regions and support private deployments in specific regions for data residency. we'll call that out in the security pack
[06:15] Alicia: how long to stand up a dedicated environment for pilot?
[06:19] Jordan: typical pilot provisioning is 1-2 weeks depending on capacity and region. if you need private on-prem that's longer: usually 4-8 weeks
[06:28] Mark: for the benchmark, we want to test both model parity and throughput on our prompt set. what's required on our side?
[06:34] Samira: we'll need a seed dataset (sample prompts + expected outputs/eval metrics), traffic profile (QPS, token distribution), and preferred region. we'll run the test and give a report
[06:45] Mark: can we do a smoke run with vLLM artifacts to see artifact compatibility?
[06:50] Samira: yes, bring a checkpoint or TGI export. we have a conversion guide; sometimes we do a quick conversion internally and run a smoke test
[06:58] Devon: procurement questions: license terms for Dedicated?
[07:02] Jordan: reserved capacity is monthly or annual commits with an SLA. pricing has per-token and per-hour GPU components; i'll include contract templates in the follow-up
[07:12] Priya: on network egress: if we do Dedicated but host in our VPC, will logs still leave our network? we need assurance on log residency

[07:20] Samira: logs can be sent to your SIEM and kept in your tenancy for private deployments. for Redwood-hosted Dedicated, we retain operational logs for support but PII and request payload retention can be controlled via config
[07:30] Mark: fine. any blockers you foresee for parity with OpenAI outputs?

[07:35] Samira: main blockers are model differences and prompt tokenization; we can often match outputs but might need small prompt rewrites and temperature tuning. also some proprietary safety filters differ, we can align on safety rules
[07:46] Alicia: whats the rollout recommendation? phased by route?
[07:50] Jordan: yes, start with low-risk routes (embeddings, batch jobs), then chat non-critical, then critical chat. use canary and monitor eval regressions
[07:58] Mark: what's the expected cost delta: very rough: if we commit to dedicated vs pure OpenAI hosted?

[08:05] Jordan: depends heavily on traffic and model family. for high QPS customers dedicated typically reduces unit cost by 30-60% versus pure hosted. we'll run a model with your numbers and give an estimate
[08:18] Devon: timeline: we're aiming to decide by end of year. is that feasible?
[08:22] Jordan: yes: pilot in December/January fits that decision timeline. we'll prioritize SOC2 docs this week
[08:30] Priya: any special notes about LLM toolkits like TGI and vLLM?

[08:35] Samira: they're common for experimentation. for Dedicated we handle the inference runtime; we can ingest vLLM outputs or host converted artifacts. performance tuning will be needed, and we'll document tuned quantization profiles
[08:48] Mark: one more technical: how do you handle cold cache spikes? our 99th spikes are mostly cold-starts for new sessions
[08:55] Samira: we do warmup pools and pre-warm frequently used models, plus prefix caching. for Critical routes we recommend reserved warm nodes or burst capacity with low spinup times
[09:10] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps
[09:13] Jordan: action 1 - jordan send pricing + security pack by thursday (2026-11-26)
[09:18] Jordan: action 2 - samira schedule benchmark and pilot run with mark (target by 2026-12-01)
[09:24] Jordan: action 3 - pulseai to share sample prompt set + eval metrics by 2026-11-30
[09:30] Alicia: sounds good, we'll share the artifacts and loop in procurement
[09:34] Devon: thanks all, excited to see the benchmark
[09:36] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs
[09:40] End of recording
